Fundamentally, we have an inherent issue in crude oil production. That’s because the Strait of Hormuz is closed, inbound tankers remain nonexistent, and Middle East producers cannot offload onshore crude oil production into tankers, thus shutting in production.

However, the market is instead focusing on product tightness because... you guessed it, product prices haven’t sold off. Pavlov’s experiment is on crude, not products, which is inherently making people think that product is where the issue is.

Now don’t misunderstand my point here: petroleum products are an issue, but China has spare refining capacity. To say that we have serious structural issues in petroleum products is like saying we don’t have enough steaks because we don’t have enough butcher shops. No man, we don’t have enough cows.

Strait of Hormuz over the last 24 hours: war is back on?

MOU on, MOU off.

Strait on, Strait off.

War on, war off.

The back and forth is getting stupid at some point, but what's not stupid is the stakes involved here. Some have incorrectly pointed out that all the US had to do was adhere to the MOU. 

No, that's wrong. 

If the US gave Iran control of the Strait of Hormuz, Iran would be the most powerful oil producer in the world. And during the MOU period, IRGC stopped issuing permits because Israel wouldn't leave Lebanon. The Strait of Hormuz is the leverage; that's why the MOU was dead on arrival. 

Looking at the video from @MarineTraffic, you can see that there are some tankers that trickle in, but they do not move the production shut-in math. UAE appears to be the only one that's getting some benefit from this, but even its export volumes in July are down ~600k b/d m-o-m.

Iraq is moving volumes, but it is likely a mixture of Iranian crude + Iraqi crude. This game has been played for years before as to evade both the blockade and sanctions.

Nonetheless, with the strikes ongoing again, the markets should come to the realization soon enough that the conflict in the Strait of Hormuz will not be solved with diplomacy. There's no way out but through.

Statement CPC

"Regarding the terrorist attack on a tanker in the waters of the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) Marine Terminal.

On July 30, 2026, at 01:48 Moscow time, the "NISSOS SIFNOS" tanker, flying the flag of the Marshall Islands and operated by Tengizchevroil LLP (a Chevron company), which was undergoing oil loading at the CPC floating loading device (FLS) No. 3, was subjected to a terrorist attack.

As a result of the attack using an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), a fire broke out in the area of the manifolds for receiving oil on the deck of the tanker. The fire was extinguished by the tanker's crew with the assistance of three CPC support vessels.

There were no casualties or injuries among CPC employees or contractors. No oil spills occurred. Medical assistance and evacuation of the tanker's crew were not requested. The tanker remained afloat, and an assessment of the damage is underway. Oil loading has been suspended, and the pipeline facilities are operating in normal mode.

In addition, another tanker, the "MARATHI," flying the flag of the Isle of Man and en route to receive oil at the CPC Marine Terminal, was also attacked in the territorial waters, 6 nautical miles from the CPC Marine Terminal.

Thus, the calls of the Republic of Kazakhstan and other foreign shareholders of CPC, including through the U.S. Department of State, regarding the inadmissibility of the use of force against international energy infrastructure, were ignored. This creates risks for global energy security, disrupts mechanisms for uninterrupted international trade in energy resources, and causes significant damage to the economic interests of the Republic of Kazakhstan and Western shareholders of CPC, as well as companies that are shippers of CPC, including Chevron, ExxonMobil, Eni, Total, Shell, and others.

Such terrorist attacks also pose a threat to the lives of international crews of marine tankers and create significant environmental risks in the Black Sea, as an attack on a tanker in the area of loading facilities could have led to the entire tanker catching fire and a major oil spill." #oott
